key_insight: Combining 3D welding simulations with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects and stabilize thermal and axial-force responses in HDPE joining.
method: Model heat, forces, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian simulation.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Simulations agreed with experimental responses and void formation; ANNs achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested welding parameters remains unestablished; new geometries or operating ranges require validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
